title: Runbook Synthesis Simulator and Adaptive Admin Advisor
creator: Maya Chen
description: Build a Runbook Synthesis Simulator (RSS) and an Adaptive Admin Advisor (AAA) that together let oncall engineers preview, dry-run, and get automated remediation suggestions for common support scenarios. The simulator will execute runbooks as first-class tasks in a sandboxed environment (no production side effects) using sampled telemetry and synthetic inputs; the advisor will surface prioritized next actions and confidence scores based on historical playbooks and incident outcomes.
acceptance_criteria:
1) The simulator can ingest a runbook (YAML/typed JSON) and run it in a sandbox against synthetic state for at least three canonical incident types (e.g., GPU OOM, model cache corruption, degraded latency).
2) No simulator execution performs network writes or mutates production resources; artifacts are isolated in ephemeral namespaces.
3) The advisor exposes a ranked list of 3 suggested next steps with confidence scores and a rationale string for each suggestion.
4) Integrations: simulator output visible in the Console runbook preview panel and the advisor widget shows for users with ops role.
5) Unit tests for the core sequencer and end-to-end smoke test against the dry-run harness are present and pass in CI.
6) Documentation (Confluence) + internal demo recorded and linked in ticket.
implementation_notes:
Design: RSS will reuse the Runlet execution engine but sandboxed—we will fork runlet-runtime with a DryRunPolicy layer that short-circuits side-effecting steps and simulates responses using a synthetic input generator. The AAA will be a scoring layer that uses runbook metadata, recent telemetry vectors from the incidents datastore, and a small logistic regression model (initially rule-weighted) to rank steps.
Architecture trade-offs considered:
- Full model-based suggestion vs rule-backed hybrid: we start hybrid to avoid opaque recommendations and enable deterministic rollbacks.
- Synthetic inputs: sample from last-30-day incident traces but cap cardinality to avoid sensitive data leaks.
Sandboxing details: ephemeral kube namespaces + mock infra adapters; use the existing ops-sandbox-perf cluster.
Telemetry: add structured event hooks to record simulated step durations and divergence from expected outputs for future tuning.
PRs: implementation will arrive as multiple PRs across repos: runlet-runtime (sandbox layer), rss-simulator service, console-integration PR.
testing_plan:
1) Unit tests for DryRunPolicy and sequencer edge cases (timeouts, missing preconditions).
2) Integration test: run three prepared canonical runbooks through simulator against synthetic traces and assert outcomes/no side effects.
3) Fuzzer: randomly mutate step inputs to check for simulator resilience and ensure no external I/O.
4) UX QA: Console panel renders results and advisor suggestions for a test user and a viewer user.
5) Load test: run 200 parallel dry-runs to validate resource limits and autoscaling behavior.
6) Post-launch: gather usage metrics and false-positive/negative rates of advisor suggestions for first 4 weeks.
rollout_plan:
Phase 1 (internal alpha): limited to SRE and oncall volunteers in ops-sandbox cluster. Collect feedback and telemetry.
Phase 2 (beta): enable in Console for all internal ops with a prominent warning and an opt-in toggle; provide training session.
Phase 3: flip on advisor suggestions for a small group of product infra teams; evaluate accuracy and incident reduction.
Fallback: advisor can be disabled per-user; simulator dry-run will always be non-destructive.
metrics:
- Simulator runs per week (target 500 in first month)
- Advisor suggestion adoption rate (% of suggestions followed)
- Suggestion precision/recall measured against post-incident remediation (target precision > 70% initially)
- Time-to-first-action reduced for incidents where advisor was used
- Sandbox resource cost per 1k dry-runs
notes:
Security: scrub synthetic traces and strip customer identifiers before feeding to simulator seeds. Compliance: coordinate with Privacy for synthetic data policy.
Open questions: how to credit suggestions in post-incident RCA? should we auto-link suggestions to runbook versioning?
